transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Well, doctor, I... I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. I know you see people with real, serious problems. But, um, my daughter insisted I come in. 

It's just... well, ever since my dear friend from choir passed away—it was so sudden, you see—I just haven't quite been myself. I mean, it's silly, really, but I find myself tearing up over the smallest things, like looking at the potluck sign-up sheets. And I get so flustered over phone calls that I used to handle without a second thought. I've even started missing some of the church planning committee meetings, which isn't like me at all. I usually never miss those. 

I'm sure it's just a phase, right? Everybody gets a little overwhelmed sometimes, don't they? I just... I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here.
Have you found that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once looked forward to, like choir or church events?

Oh, well, I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest. I mean, I still love my choir and my church family, of course. It's just... well, maybe I haven't been quite as enthusiastic as usual lately. 

I suppose I have been staying home a bit more, but that's just because I've been a little tired, you know? Not because I don't care. I still want to go to everything, I really do. I just... I haven't quite had the energy to be my usual cheerful self at the gatherings, so I thought it might be better to just sit a few out until I'm back to normal. That makes sense, doesn't it? I don't want to be a burden or bring anyone else down.
Would you say that your mood has been generally low or sad, even when you're not thinking about your friend who passed away?

Oh, goodness, no, I don't think so. I mean... I really try my best to keep a smile on my face, especially for my family. When I'm keeping busy around the house or talking to my daughter about her day, I feel... well, I feel fine, mostly. 

It's really just when something reminds me of her, or when I have a little too much quiet time to think, that I get a bit teary. But I'm certainly not just sitting around feeling sad all day for no reason, I promise. I always try to look on the bright side of things and count my blessings... that's the best way to handle it, don't you think?
Have you noticed that you've been feeling more tired or low on energy, even when you're not doing anything physically taxing?

Well, maybe a little bit, but I think that's just normal for someone my age, right? I mean, I'm certainly not as spry as I was in my thirties! 

I do get a little worn out sometimes, but I always make sure to get my chores done. I'm not... I'm not just lying in bed all day or anything like that. I still keep a very tidy house. It's just that sometimes, maybe around mid-afternoon, I feel like I need to sit down for a spell with a cup of tea. But that's perfectly acceptable, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm not making a fuss over nothing. I'm sure everyone gets a little tired now and then.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than usual?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I've always been a pretty good sleeper, thankfully. I mean, maybe once in a great while I'll wake up to use the restroom in the middle of the night, but at my age, well, I think everyone does that, don't they? 

I usually just go right back to sleep without any fuss. I certainly wouldn't say I'm tossing and turning or having any real trouble. I always make sure to get a good night's rest so I can be ready for the next day and not be a bother to anyone. You don't need to worry about my sleep at all, doctor. That's a good thing, right? I'm really trying my best to take care of myself.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating more or less than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Oh, no, my appetite is just fine, thank you for checking. I still make all my usual meals, and I eat them right on schedule. I mean, I'm not a big eater anyway, never have been, really. 

My clothes all still fit exactly the same, so I haven't lost or gained any weight. I always try to eat a balanced diet—plenty of vegetables and not too many sweets—so I can stay healthy and not end up at the doctor's office for something silly! I'm doing all the right things there, I promise. It's so important to keep your strength up, don't you agree?
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or remember things lately?

Oh, my memory is sharp as a tack, I assure you. I keep a very organized calendar on the fridge, and I never miss an appointment or a birthday. 

I suppose sometimes I might walk into a room and forget what I went in there for, but... well, goodness, that happens to everyone, doesn't it? I just retrace my steps and it comes right back to me. I'm certainly not sitting around confused or anything like that. I manage my own checkbook and pay all my bills on time. I try very hard to stay on top of things so I don't become a burden to my children. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I'm supposed to be doing.
Have you found yourself thinking more about death or dying lately, or felt like life isn’t worth living?

Oh, my goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I would never... I mean, I know some people struggle with those kinds of thoughts, but I'm very grateful for my life, I really am. 

I try to look on the bright side of things, you know? I have my children, and I want to be around for them for a long, long time. I would never want to put them through anything like that. I'm a very positive person, mostly. I always try to keep a smile on my face and just keep moving forward. That's the best way to handle things, don't you think? Just counting your blessings and staying strong? I promise you, doctor, you don't need to worry about me in that regard. I'm doing just fine.
Do you find yourself worrying more than usual about everyday things, like health, family, or responsibilities, even when there’s no clear reason to be concerned?

Oh, well... I suppose I worry a little bit, but just the normal amount, really. You know, making sure the house is tidy, hoping the kids are doing well at their jobs, that sort of thing. Nothing out of the ordinary. 

I mean, I don't sit around wringing my hands all day or anything like that. I just like to make sure everything is taken care of properly. It's just being responsible, isn't it? A mother's job is never really done, even when they're grown. I try very hard not to fuss over them too much, though. I know they have their own lives. I'm just being a caring parent, right? That's completely normal, don't you think?
Have you found yourself feeling particularly anxious or worried about things related to your friend’s passing or other events since then, even when there’s no clear reason for concern?

Well... I suppose I have been a little more flustered lately, but I'm trying very hard to keep it together. Ever since my friend from the choir passed away so suddenly, I just... I haven't quite been myself. 

I mean, it's silly, really, but I find myself crying over the simplest things, like looking at the potluck sign-up sheets. And I get all worked up about phone calls that I used to handle with no problem at all. I've even started missing some of the church planning committee meetings, which I never, ever used to do. I feel terrible about it, I really do. I know I should be handling things better, and I'm trying my best not to let it affect my responsibilities. It's just taking me a little longer to bounce back than I thought it would. That's understandable after losing a friend, isn't it? I'm sure I'll be back to my old self soon enough, don't you think?
Would you say that your worries or anxiety have been constant, even when there’s no immediate reason for them, and do they feel difficult to control at times?

Oh, no, no... I wouldn't say it's constant. Goodness, no. I mean, I don't want you to think I'm just a bundle of nerves all day long! 

Like I mentioned, I have my moments when I'm reminded of my friend, or when I have to deal with the church committee, but I'm certainly not just sitting around worrying for absolutely no reason. When I'm keeping busy around the house or watching my evening programs, I feel perfectly fine. I can usually pull myself together when I really need to. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or losing control of myself. It's really just tied to the grief, you know? Just those little reminders that catch me off guard. But otherwise, I think I'm managing it reasonably well. I'm doing my best to stay grounded, anyway. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I can still enjoy my quiet time at home?

Would you say that your anxiety or worry continues even when you're not thinking about your friend’s passing or specific events at church, and does it sometimes feel like it’s just there all the time, even without a clear cause?

Oh, well... no, not really. I mean, if I'm not thinking about my friend or, you know, the church things... I'm usually okay. 

I really don't think it's just hanging over me for no reason at all. Like I said, if I'm just sitting quietly or tending to my plants, I feel quite calm, actually. I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm just anxious all the time about nothing. It really does seem to just be when those sad thoughts creep in, or when I feel like I'm letting people down at the church. 

I'm doing my very best to keep a positive outlook otherwise. It's perfectly normal to only feel upset when you're reminded of something sad, isn't it? I think I'm handling the rest of my day just fine.

Have you noticed any moments where you feel anxious or worried when you're not thinking about your friend, church responsibilities, or anything specific—just a general sense of worry without a clear cause?

Oh, dear... I'm so sorry, I feel like I must not be explaining myself very well. I hope I'm not frustrating you with my answers. But truly, no... I don't have that sort of general worry. 

I promise I'm not just walking around feeling anxious out of the blue or for no reason at all. It really is only tied to losing my friend and, well, the guilt over stepping back from my church duties. If I'm just baking or folding my laundry, my mind is perfectly quiet and I feel just fine. 

I'm trying to be as helpful as I can... am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, doctor.
When something reminds you of your friend’s passing, do you find that your anxiety or sadness feels more intense or lasts much longer than you would expect?

Well... I suppose it's hard to say what's expected, isn't it? I mean, losing someone so dear... it's bound to hurt. 

I don't think I'm overreacting, if that's what you mean. I really hope it doesn't seem that way. When I see a picture of her, or... or someone mentions her name, I do get sad, of course. I might shed a tear or need a moment to myself. But I don't think it lasts an unusually long time. I try very hard to pull myself together quickly so I'm not a bother to anyone around me. 

I mean, it's just normal grief, right? I'm not... I'm not being overly dramatic about it, am I? I just try to let the moment pass and get back to whatever I was doing. I think I'm handling those reminders as best as anyone could expect.
Have you noticed any times when you feel anxious or worried even when nothing specific is happening or there’s no clear reason for it?

Oh, goodness, I... I feel like we might have just talked about this, and I really hope I'm not being difficult or confusing you. I'm trying my best to answer correctly. 

But, um, no. I don't get anxious just out of the blue, when nothing is going on. I really don't. Like I mentioned, if I'm just going about my day, doing my chores or sitting quietly, I'm perfectly fine. I don't want you to think I'm just a bundle of nerves all the time for no reason. 

It's really just the sadness about my friend, and feeling bad about the church. That's all it is. I'm doing okay otherwise, I promise. Is that... is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

Can you think of a time recently when you weren’t thinking about your friend, church, or any specific problem, and yet still felt a sense of anxiety or worry? Just a general feeling, even for a short while, without a clear cause?

Oh, dear... I, um... I feel terrible, because I think you're asking me the same thing again, and that must mean I'm just not explaining myself properly. I'm so sorry if I'm wasting your time or not being clear. 

But... no, I really can't think of a time like that. I promise I'm thinking very hard about it! But if I'm not thinking about... well, about her, or about letting everyone down at the church... I just don't feel that way. I'm not sitting around worrying about nothing, I swear I'm not. 

I hope that's okay to say. I just... I want to give you the right answer, but I really don't have those kinds of general worries. Am I making any sense at all? I feel awful that we keep having to go over this.

Can you think of a time when you weren’t focused on your friend’s passing, church, or any particular issue, and yet you still felt a sense of anxiety or worry that didn’t seem to go away, even for a little while?

Oh, Doctor, I am so, so sorry. I feel like I'm frustrating you, and that is the absolute last thing I want to do. I know you're just trying to help me, and I must be doing a terrible job of answering your questions if you have to keep asking me the same thing. 

I'm really trying to dig deep and find an example for you, I truly am. But... I just don't have one. If my mind isn't on my friend or the church, I'm... I'm really quite alright. I don't have this lingering worry or anxiety about nothing. I just don't. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm failing this somehow by not giving you the answer you're looking for. Please don't be upset with me. I'm just trying to be as honest as I can be. Is it... is it very bad that I don't feel that way?
Can you think of any time in the past few weeks when you weren't thinking about your friend, the church, or any specific problem, and yet still felt anxious or worried, even for a short while?

Oh, my... Doctor, I... I really don't know what else to say, and I feel just terrible because I can tell I'm not giving you the answer you need for your notes. I am so, so sorry. I really am trying to be a good patient for you, I promise. 

But... no. Honestly, no. If my mind is occupied with a television program, or I'm just folding laundry and not thinking about... well, about my friend or the church... I'm perfectly calm. I'm really not a nervous person by nature, I'm just going through a hard time with this one specific thing. 

I hope you aren't upset with me for repeating myself again. Is there... maybe a different way I should be thinking about your question? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and being helpful to you.
